profile.summary: This is a Rewire-built calibration benchmark, not a published suite. It takes precomputed scores from eight variant predictors and foundation models and converts them into ACMG/AMP computational evidence thresholds (PP3 and BP4, from +1 to +8 and -1 to -8) using the Pejaver et al. 2022 local posterior method with the Bergquist et al. 2025 additions. The scoring set is ClinVar GRCh38 missense SNVs with at least two review stars that were not classified P/LP or B/LB in the 26 December 2023 ClinVar release (or the 30 March 2025 release for the sensitivity cohort). It runs on CPU from committed score tables.

summary_quotes.text: Calibrates genomic foundation models and clinical variant-effect predictors into ACMG/AMP computational evidence thresholds (`PP3` and `BP4`, points `+1` to `+8` and `-1` to `-8`) on temporally held-out ClinVar GRCh38 missense SNVs using CPU-only precomputed score tables.

**Calibration framework**: Pejaver et al. 2022 (`PMC9748256`, disease prior `alpha = 0.0441`, `c = 1124`, `minpoints = 100`, gnomAD population reference fraction `gft = 0.03`) combined with Bergquist et al. 2025
excluding all variants classified P/LP or B/LB in `clinvar_20231226.vcf.gz`

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Two things at once. First, how well each predictor separates pathogenic or likely pathogenic from benign or likely benign missense variants, reported as AUROC with a 95% interval and AUPRC. Second, and the point of the exercise, which ACMG/AMP evidence strengths each predictor's scores can actually support: the score value at which the local posterior probability of pathogenicity reaches the cutoff for supporting, moderate, intermediate, strong and very strong evidence, in both directions. Where a predictor's scores never reach a strength on a cohort, the table records that it was not reached.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Variants come from the ClinVar GRCh38 VCF of 8 November 2026, restricted to clean missense SNVs with at least two review stars. Three cohorts are drawn. post_2023_12 is the primary one: 9,450 variants (5,508 pathogenic or likely pathogenic, 3,942 benign or likely benign), of which 4,188 are new since 26 December 2023, excluding every variant already classified P/LP or B/LB in the December 2023 release. post_2023_12_af001 restricts the same cohort to 8,141 variants whose gnomAD v3.1.2 non-1000G genome grpmax frequency is below 0.1%. post_2025_03 is a sensitivity cohort of 3,818 variants held out from 30 March 2025. A separate population reference set of 6,312 missense SNVs (5,155 ClinVar variants of uncertain significance with population frequency and 1,157 gnomAD background SNVs), disjoint from the evaluation cohorts, supplies the population term the calibration needs.

`post_2023_12_af001` (AF-controlled): `8,141` missense SNVs (`5,454` P/LP, `2,687` B/LB) with gnomAD v3.1.2 `grpmax < 0.1%`.
`post_2025_03` (sensitivity): `3,818` ClinVar `2026-11-08` `>=2-star` missense SNVs (`2,306` P/LP, `1,512` B/LB; `1,134` novel since `2025-03-30`)
`gnomad_ref_missense`: `6,312` population reference missense SNVs (`5,155` ClinVar VUS with population AF and `1,157` gnomAD missense background SNVs, disjoint from held-out evaluation cohorts).

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: The calibration uses a disease prior alpha of 0.0441, c of 1124, a minimum of 100 points per local window and a population reference fraction gft of 0.03, following Pejaver et al. 2022. Bergquist et al. 2025 adds the +3 and -3 intermediate strengths and one-sided 95% conservative discounted thresholds from 1,000 bootstrap resamples, with seed 20261123. The posterior cutoffs that define each strength are recorded in the output (for example 0.0999 for supporting and 0.6073 for strong). The run took 173.51 seconds on CPU, and the receipt records the hash of every input score table and every output file.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: The calibration re-runs from the committed cohort and score tables with one command and no GPU, then the result hashes can be checked against the committed SHA256SUMS file. A test suite covers the calculation and the file integrity.

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: Three evaluation cohorts drawn from the ClinVar 8 November 2026 GRCh38 release: post_2023_12 (9,450 variants), post_2023_12_af001 (8,141) and post_2025_03 (3,818), plus a population reference set of 6,312 missense SNVs. Nine score tracks across eight predictors are calibrated.

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Temporal holdout, not train and test: each cohort keeps only variants not classified P/LP or B/LB in an earlier ClinVar release (26 December 2023 or 30 March 2025). The population reference set is disjoint from the evaluation cohorts.

quotes.text: excluding all variants classified P/LP or B/LB in `clinvar_20231226.vcf.gz`
excluding variants classified P/LP or B/LB in `clinvar_20250330.vcf.gz`

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: AUROC with a 95% interval and AUPRC (higher is better), plus the calibrated score threshold for each evidence strength (bp4_strong_4 through pp3_very_strong_8) and the share of pathogenic variants reaching PP3 supporting or strong and of benign variants reaching BP4 supporting or moderate.

quotes.text: stratum	predictor	role	n_pos	n_neg	auroc	auroc_lo	auroc_hi	auprc

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: Clinical predictors AlphaMissense, REVEL v1.3 and CADD v1.7 (PHRED) are the reference points for the foundation models GPN-MSA, GPN-Star vertebrate v100, GPN-Star mammal m447 and AlphaGenome AVI (raw and PHRED). EVEE is included only as a leaked descriptive control.

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Two. A temporal cutoff removes variants already classified in the earlier ClinVar release. An allele-frequency control restricts benign variants in post_2023_12_af001 to gnomAD v3.1.2 non-1000G genome grpmax below 0.1%, so common polymorphisms do not make pathogenic separation look easier. EVEE is known to be exposed to ClinVar supervision through 20 March 2026 and is withheld from the unconfounded comparison for that reason.

quotes.text: rare variants in `post_2023_12_af001` are restricted to gnomAD v3.1.2 non-1000G-overlapping genome `grpmax < 0.1%` (`0.001`) queried via MyVariant.info so benign common polymorphisms do not flatter pathogenic separation

incorporates ClinVar supervision through `2026-03-20` and therefore has direct target exposure on the `post_2023_12` and `post_2025_03` cohorts. It is included solely as a descriptive leaked control and withheld from unconfounded model comparisons.

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: 1,000 bootstrap resamples with seed 20261123 give one-sided 95% conservative discounted thresholds, and AUROC is reported with a 95% interval (for example 0.863 with 0.855 to 0.870 for GPN-MSA on post_2023_12).

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: No assay: labels are ClinVar clinical classifications with at least two review stars, and the population term uses gnomAD allele frequencies.

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: Precomputed score tables only: one committed TSV per predictor, so nothing is run from sequence. The receipt lists the eight score files and their hashes.

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: None of the predictors is trained or fine-tuned here. The calibration itself fits thresholds from the held-out cohort and the population reference set.

strengths.text: The output is in the units a clinical laboratory uses: a score threshold per ACMG/AMP evidence strength, rather than an AUROC alone.

notes: This is a Rewire study, not a third-party benchmark: the code, cohorts, score tables and results all live in rewire-bio/rewire-benchmarks under benchmarks/clingen-pp3-bp4, under MIT. The three structured entries match the store's three protocols. released is the completion date in the execution receipt (2026-11-23), not a publication date. AUROC is given as the primary metric because it is the one comparable number across predictors; the point of the benchmark is the per-strength thresholds, which are not a single metric. The methods it implements are published elsewhere (Pejaver et al. 2022, PMC9748256, and Bergquist et al. 2025, PMC12208618); neither paper was fetched for this page, so the description of the calibration is taken from this benchmark's own README. The cohort and score TSV files were not downloaded; their hashes are in the receipt.
